description: Freeze section tube (2-in drain/isolation line; FV-101 FV-103 FV-104)
notes: FV-101: primary drain valve (de-energise-to-open). FV-103: fill valve (energise-to-open). FV-104: secondary drain isolation valve between reactor vessel lower nozzle and FV-101 (series with FV-101; normally frozen/closed; provides second passive drain actuation point for defence-in-depth). No insulation on this section; butt-weld ends; smooth exterior for heater wire winding.

notes: Wound on freeze section at ~30 turns per 25 mm; resist = ~29 Ω total for 500 W at 120V

notes: Encapsulates heater wire on freeze section; electrically isolating; cured at 120 C before first use

specification: Thermon or Chromalox MI cable; rated 700 C; 2-conductor
notes: From heater winding terminals to junction box outside insulation; ~500 mm each

specification: MI thermocouple; 3.2 mm OD sheath; 300 mm lg; IEC 60584 Class 1
notes: 2 per valve (redundant); welded well or press-against fitting on freeze section surface. Type N (Nicrosil/Nisil) selected for superior oxidation resistance at 450–650°C compared to Type K (Chromel) in fluoride-vapour environment. Hastelloy-N sheath (UNS N10003) replaces Inconel 600 for compatibility in salt-adjacent service. REPLACEMENT INTERVAL: Every 18 months or on drift >10°C from reference — whichever comes first.
One per valve; contains terminal strips for heater power and TC connections; outdoor rated
